cards.explanation: The answer is to buy grain so they can live. Jacob, the father of these brothers, says it plainly: “Go down there and buy some for us, so that we may live and not die.” (Genesis 42:2) Life is on the line, and the errand is just as clear. One job, friends, and it's buying grain. No side quests.

The answer is ten. Verse 3 says it straight: “So ten of Joseph’s brothers went down to buy grain from Egypt.” Ten brothers is a lot of people for one shopping list. Benjamin isn't in that number, as the next verse shows (Genesis 42:4).

The answer is Benjamin. Verse 4 says, “But Jacob did not send Joseph’s brother Benjamin with his brothers…” Benjamin is the brother Jacob keeps close to home. The ten go and he stays. You can tell Jacob has his eye on this one.

The answer is False. Nothing here says Benjamin is needed for the flocks. Jacob says, “I am afraid that harm might befall him.” (Genesis 42:4) The reason is a father's fear, friends. No job posting involved.

The answer is that they bow with their faces to the ground. Verse 6 says that when the brothers arrived, “…they bowed down before him with their faces to the ground.” Joseph was the ruler of the land, the one selling the grain. Ten men bowing low in front of him, and verse 8 says they did not recognize him (Genesis 42:8).

The answers are strangers and harshly. Verse 7 says Joseph “…recognized them, but he treated them as strangers…” He knows exactly who they are, and he plays like he's never met them. That's a lot of poker face for one man standing in front of his own brothers. The text says Joseph “…spoke harshly to them.” (Genesis 42:7)

The answer is spies. Joseph says, “You are spies! You have come to see if our land is vulnerable.” (Genesis 42:9) He goes straight from a question to an accusation. The brothers came for grain and left that conversation with a spy charge.

The answer is twelve. The brothers say, “Your servants are twelve brothers, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan.” (Genesis 42:13) They count all twelve, even the one they say is gone. The man they're talking to is one of those twelve. He just heard himself counted.

The answer is True. The brothers tell Joseph, “The youngest is now with our father…” (Genesis 42:13) They're talking about Benjamin, who stayed home with Jacob. That detail turns out to matter a lot in what Joseph says next.

The answer is that their youngest brother comes here. Joseph swears, “As surely as Pharaoh lives, you shall not leave this place unless your youngest brother comes here.” (Genesis 42:15) Pharaoh is Egypt's king, and Joseph uses his life as the oath. This is how he says the brothers will be tested. The test starts with one name: the youngest.

The answer is just one of them. In the new deal, Joseph says, “…leave one of your brothers in custody while the rest of you go and take back grain…” (Genesis 42:19) That's a big drop from the plan where nearly everyone stayed locked up. One brother stays and the others head home.

The answer is False. The brothers keep the grain. Joseph tells them to “…go and take back grain to relieve the hunger of your households.” (Genesis 42:19) The households back home need that food. The grain makes the trip with them.

The answer is what they did to their brother. They say, “Surely we are being punished because of our brother. We saw his anguish when he pleaded with us, but we would not listen.” (Genesis 42:21) Their trouble in Egypt gets tied right back to how they treated him. They remember his pleading and say they would not listen.

The answer is Reuben. Verse 22 says Reuben responded, “Didn’t I tell you not to sin against the boy? But you would not listen.” (Genesis 42:22) Reuben is one of the brothers standing there. He's the one reminding everybody that he spoke up.

The answer is True. Verse 23 says, “They did not realize that Joseph understood them, since there was an interpreter between them.” So they have no idea he understands. I think that's a very quiet kind of hard.

The answer is Simeon. Verse 24 says Joseph “…took Simeon from them and had him bound before their eyes.” Simeon is the brother who stays. The others have to watch it happen, and I think that's a hard thing to watch.

The answer is silver. Verse 25 says Joseph gave orders “…to return each man’s silver to his sack…” So the bags get filled with grain, and the silver goes right back in the sacks. I bet somebody's in for a surprise when a sack gets opened.

The answer is that their hearts sink and they tremble. Verse 28 says, “Their hearts sank, and trembling, they turned to one another…” Finding the silver doesn't feel like good news to them. They ask, “What is this that God has done to us?”

The answer is their brother back and the right to trade. The brothers repeat the man's words to Jacob: “Then I will give your brother back to you, and you can trade in the land.” (Genesis 42:34) Their brother comes back, and they can trade there. It comes with a condition, which is bringing the youngest brother back to him.
The answer is True. Verse 35 says that when they and their father saw the bags of silver, “…they were dismayed.” Jacob and his sons all feel it. Nobody's throwing a party over that silver, friends.

The answer is “Everything is going against me!” (Genesis 42:36) Jacob says it right after naming Joseph gone and Simeon no more, with Benjamin now on the table. That's a lot of loss in one sentence. I think he feels it all at once.

The answer is that Jacob can kill Reuben's two sons. Reuben says, “You may kill my two sons…” (Genesis 42:37) That's a heavy thing to put on the table. I think he wants Jacob to see how serious he is about bringing Benjamin back. He also says, “Put him in my care, and I will return him.”

The answer is False. Jacob refuses. He says, “My son will not go down there with you, for his brother is dead, and he alone is left.” (Genesis 42:38) Reuben made his offer, and Jacob's answer is still no. The story isn't over, though.
